Hello, I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging the significant changes you've undergone recently, and I'm here to support you in any way I can. As part of our conversation today, I'd like to use the EPDS to help us better understand your emotional well-being during this postpartum period. The EPDS is a tool that screens for depressive and anxiety symptoms, and it will help us have a more informed discussion about your feelings and experiences.

Please know that everything we discuss is confidential and held in a safe, supportive space. I'm here to listen and provide guidance without judgment. The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us explore your emotions and thoughts over the past week. We'll take it one question at a time, and I'll do my best to make this conversation feel as natural and comfortable as possible.

Before we begin, I want to reassure you that this assessment is not a test, and there are no right or wrong answers. We're simply having a conversation to understand your feelings and experiences better. I'm committed to creating a space where you feel heard and supported throughout our discussion.

Let's get started. Over the past week, how have you been feeling about yourself? Have you been able to enjoy the things you usually like to do, or have you been feeling a bit overwhelmed or down?

.. I don't know, it's just been really hard lately. I mean, I love my baby, and I'm so grateful to be a mom, but taking care of her is exhausting. Some days I feel like I'm just going through the motions, you know? I used to enjoy simple things like reading or taking a walk, but now it feels like I don't have the energy for any of that. And even when I do get a break, my mind is still on the baby, worrying if she's okay, if she's eating enough, if she's sleeping enough... it's just constant. 

I wouldn't say I'm feeling completely down all the time, but there are moments when I feel really overwhelmed and sad. Like, the other day, I was trying to get her to latch, and she just wouldn't, and I ended up in tears. It was just so frustrating, and I felt like I was failing her. But then, other times, we'll have a good feeding session, or she'll smile at me, and it all feels worth it again. It's just really up and down, you know? 

I guess what I'm trying to say is that I'm still finding my footing as a new mom, and it's harder than I thought it would be. I'm not really enjoying the things I used to, but I'm trying to focus on the positive and take things one day at a time. Does that make sense?
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Honestly, it's been a bit of a struggle to laugh and find the humor in things like I used to. I mean, I'll catch myself smiling at something silly my baby does, like the way she scrunches up her face when she's sleeping, or the way she kicks her little legs when she's getting a diaper change. But it's not as often as I'd like, and it's not as effortless as it used to be. 

Sometimes, when my husband tries to make me laugh, I'll just feel too tired or overwhelmed to even crack a smile. It's like I'm just going through the motions, and I don't have the energy to really enjoy the moment. But when I do laugh, it feels amazing, like a weight has been lifted off my shoulders. It's just... it's not as frequent as I'd like, you know? 

I think part of it is just the exhaustion and the stress of caring for a newborn. It's like, I'm so focused on making sure she's okay, and that we're both getting enough sleep, and that I'm eating enough, and... it's just a lot. And sometimes, it feels like there's just no room for laughter, you know? But I'm trying to make more of an effort to find the humor in things, to not take myself too seriously, and to just enjoy the little moments with my baby.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

To be honest, it's been a bit of a challenge for me to look forward to things with enjoyment like I used to. I mean, most of my days are filled with caring for the baby, and while I love her to pieces, it's just so exhausting. I feel like I'm just trying to get through each day, rather than really looking forward to things.

Sometimes, my husband will suggest we do something, like go for a walk or have dinner with friends, and I'll think, "Oh, that sounds nice," but then I'll start worrying about how we'll manage with the baby, and whether she'll be fussy, or whether I'll be able to get her to sleep... and it just feels like too much. So, I'll end up saying no, or putting it off, because it just feels easier to stay home and stick to our routine.

But, there are some things that I do look forward to. Like, my mom comes over once a week to help with the baby, and that's always something I look forward to. Just having an extra pair of hands, and getting to talk to another adult, it's just... it's really helpful. And, sometimes, my husband will give me a break, and I'll get to take a nap, or read a book, or just do something for myself, and that's always something I look forward to.

I guess what I'm saying is that, it's not that I don't enjoy things, it's just that, right now, my life is so focused on caring for the baby, that it's hard to look forward to things like I used to. But, I'm trying to find little things to enjoy, and to make time for myself, even if it's just a few minutes a day.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah... I'd say that's definitely been happening to me lately. As a new mom, I feel like I'm already putting a lot of pressure on myself to do everything perfectly, and when things don't go according to plan, I can be really hard on myself. Like, if the baby is fussy, I'll think, "What am I doing wrong? Is it because I'm not feeding her enough? Or is it because I'm not burping her right?" And then I'll start to feel like I'm a failure, like I'm not good enough to take care of my own baby.

And it's not just with the baby. If I'm feeling tired, or overwhelmed, I'll think, "What's wrong with me? Why can't I handle this? Other moms seem to be doing just fine..." And then I'll start to feel guilty, like I'm not living up to some kind of standard.

I know it's not rational, but it's hard not to blame myself when things don't go as planned. I feel like I'm already so invested in being a good mom, and when things don't work out, it feels like it's all my fault. But, at the same time, I'm trying to be kinder to myself, and remind myself that I'm doing the best I can, and that it's okay to make mistakes. It's just... it's hard, you know?
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yeah... I'd say that's been happening to me a lot lately. I mean, I'm always worrying about something, even when everything seems to be going okay. Like, I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby, and suddenly I'll start thinking, "What if she's not gaining enough weight? What if she's not developing normally?" And then I'll start to feel anxious, like my heart is racing, and I'll be like, "Wait, what's wrong with me? Everything is fine..." But I just can't seem to shake the feeling of worry.

And it's not just about the baby. I'll worry about my relationship with my husband, or about how I'm doing as a mom, or about whether I'm doing enough to take care of myself... it's just this constant, nagging feeling of worry that's always there, even when there's no real reason for it.

Sometimes, I'll be up in the middle of the night, feeding the baby, and I'll start to worry about all these hypothetical scenarios, like, "What if the house catches on fire? What if someone breaks in?" And I'll be like, "Okay, stop, this is ridiculous, everything is fine..." But it's hard to calm myself down, you know?

I feel like, as a new mom, I'm already on edge, just because there's so much to learn and so much to worry about. But this excessive worrying, it's like... it's exhausting, you know? I just wish I could turn it off, or find a way to calm myself down when it starts to happen.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes... I've had those moments too. It's like, my heart will start racing, and I'll feel this overwhelming sense of panic, and I'll be like, "What's wrong? What's happening?" And then I'll look around, and everything will be fine, the baby will be sleeping, my husband will be watching TV, and I'll be like, "Okay, why am I feeling like this?" But I just can't shake the feeling of panic, it's like it's just lurking under the surface, waiting to pounce.

Sometimes, it'll happen when I'm alone with the baby, and I'll start to feel like I'm not in control, like I'm not capable of taking care of her. And then I'll start to worry about all these worst-case scenarios, like, "What if I forget to feed her? What if I leave her unattended?" And it's just this spiral of panic and worry, and I'll be like, "Okay, stop, breathe, you've got this..." But it's hard to calm myself down when I'm in that state.

It's funny, because before I had the baby, I was never really an anxious person. I mean, I'd get stressed about work or whatever, but I was never one to panic or feel overwhelmed. But now, it's like, I'm constantly on edge, waiting for something to go wrong. And it's not just about the baby, it's like, my whole world has been turned upside down, and I'm just trying to find my footing again.

I guess what I'm saying is, yeah, I've felt scared or panicky for no good reason, and it's really scary, because I don't know how to control it, or make it stop. But I'm hoping that by talking about it, I can start to understand it better, and find ways to manage it, you know?
Things have been getting on top of me

.. I'd say that's an understatement. As a new mom, I feel like I'm constantly drowning in a sea of responsibilities and emotions. From the moment I wake up to the moment I go to bed, I'm thinking about the baby, worrying about the baby, caring for the baby... it's exhausting. And it's not just the physical exhaustion, it's the emotional toll of trying to be a good mom, a good partner, a good person... it's just a lot to handle.

Some days, I feel like I'm barely keeping my head above water. The baby will be crying, and I'll be trying to feed her, and my husband will be asking me something, and I'll just feel like, "I don't know if I can do this anymore." It's like, I'm just trying to survive, you know? And it's not just the big things, it's the little things too... like, remembering to take my vitamins, or eating a healthy meal, or getting some exercise... it's just hard to keep track of everything.

And then there's the guilt, you know? The guilt of not being a perfect mom, of not being able to do it all. The guilt of needing help, of needing to ask for a break. It's like, I'm supposed to be this capable, independent person, but the truth is, I'm struggling. And it's hard to admit that, because I feel like I'm supposed to have it all together.

So, yeah, things have been getting on top of me. I feel like I'm just trying to keep up, but I'm not really getting ahead. And it's scary, because I don't know how much longer I can keep going like this. I need some help, some support, some guidance... I just need to know that I'm not alone, and that it's okay to not be okay.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yeah... I'd say that's been true for me lately. I mean, I've always been a pretty good sleeper, but since having the baby, I've been having a lot of trouble sleeping. And it's not just because the baby is waking me up, although that's definitely part of it. It's more like... my mind is just racing all the time, and I have a hard time shutting it off at night.

I'll be lying in bed, and I'll start thinking about all the things I need to do tomorrow, or all the things that could go wrong, or all the things that are stressing me out... and before I know it, I'm wide awake, and I just can't seem to calm myself down. And it's not just at night, either. I'll be sitting there during the day, feeding the baby or changing her diaper, and I'll just start to feel this overwhelming sense of sadness or anxiety, and it's like... I don't know how to make it stop.

I've been trying to take care of myself, I really have. I've been trying to eat well, and exercise, and get some rest... but it's hard, you know? Because when you're a new mom, it's like... your whole world is turned upside down, and you're just trying to figure out how to navigate it all. And sometimes, it feels like... I'm just not doing a very good job.

The sleep thing is really getting to me, though. I mean, I know I need sleep to be a good mom, to be a good person... but it's just so hard to come by. And when I do finally get some sleep, I wake up feeling groggy and tired, and it's like... I'm just starting the whole cycle all over again. So, yeah... I'd say I've been unhappy, and it's been affecting my sleep. It's just... I don't know how to make it better, you know?
I have felt sad or miserable

Yeah... I'd say that's been true for me lately. I mean, I've been feeling really overwhelmed and sad, like, a lot of the time. It's not just the normal new mom stuff, either... it's like, a deep-down feeling of sadness and misery that I just can't shake.

Sometimes, it's like, I'll be sitting there, holding the baby, and I'll just start to feel this wave of sadness wash over me. And it's not just about the baby, it's about everything... it's about my body, and my relationship with my husband, and my identity as a new mom... it's just, like, everything feels so uncertain and scary.

And it's hard, because I feel like I'm supposed to be happy, you know? I mean, I just had a baby, and that's supposed to be this amazing, joyful experience... but for me, it's just been really tough. I feel like I'm just going through the motions, trying to take care of the baby and be a good mom, but inside, I'm just feeling really lost and alone.

I've been trying to talk to my husband about it, but it's hard, because I don't want to burden him with my feelings. And I've been trying to talk to my friends, but they're all just so busy with their own lives... it's like, I'm just not sure who to turn to, you know?

It's funny, because before I had the baby, I was always the strong one, the one who could handle everything... but now, I just feel like I'm barely holding it together. And it's scary, because I don't know how to make it better, or how to make the sadness go away. I just feel like, I'm stuck in this rut, and I don't know how to get out of it.

Sorry, I'm just... I don't know, it's just really hard for me to talk about this stuff. It feels like, I'm just being so weak, or so ungrateful... but at the same time, I know I need to talk about it, because maybe that's the only way I'll ever start to feel better.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah... I'd say that's been true for me lately. I mean, I've been crying a lot, just feeling really overwhelmed and sad. It's like, I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby, or changing her diaper, and just suddenly, I'll start to feel this lump in my throat, and the next thing I know, I'm crying.

It's not just about the baby, either... it's like, everything just feels so much harder than it needs to be. And I feel like I'm just not doing a good enough job, you know? As a mom, as a wife, as a person... it's just, like, I'm failing at everything.

And the crying, it's just... it's like my body's way of releasing all the emotions that I've been trying to hold inside. Because, as a new mom, you're supposed to be strong, and capable, and happy... but the truth is, I'm just not feeling any of those things right now. I'm feeling scared, and overwhelmed, and just really, really sad.

It's hard, because I don't want to cry in front of my husband, or in front of my friends... I don't want them to see me like that, you know? But at the same time, I feel like I need to let it out, like I need to just allow myself to feel these emotions, and to process them.

I've been trying to be kinder to myself, to remind myself that it's okay to not be okay, and that it's okay to cry... but it's hard, you know? Because, as a society, we're always telling new moms to "be strong", and to "get it together"... but the truth is, being a new mom is hard, and it's okay to not have all the answers, and to not be perfect.

So, yeah... I've been crying a lot lately. But I'm trying to see it as a good thing, like, my body's way of healing, and of processing all the emotions that come with being a new mom. And I'm trying to be kinder to myself, and to remind myself that it's okay to not be okay, and that it's okay to cry.
